quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I believe the experiment was conducted without proper oversight.'
options: She said she believed the experiment had been conducted without proper oversight.
She said she believed the experiment was conducted without proper oversight.
She said she believes the experiment had been conducted without proper oversight.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she believed the experiment had been conducted without proper oversight.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I believe the experiment was conducted without proper oversight.'
quests.hint: 'Believe' → 'believed'. 'Was conducted' → 'had been conducted'. The embedded passive also shifts.
quests.explanation: 'Believe' → 'believed'. The embedded passive 'was conducted' → 'had been conducted'. Both the main verb and the embedded passive must shift.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The chairman asked, 'Why hasn't the report been circulated to all board members?'
options: The chairman demanded to know why the report hadn't been circulated to all board members.
The chairman demanded to know why hasn't the report been circulated to all board members.
The chairman demanded to know why the report hasn't been circulated to all board members.
quests.correctAnswer: The chairman demanded to know why the report hadn't been circulated to all board members.
quests.sentence: The chairman asked, 'Why hasn't the report been circulated to all board members?'
quests.hint: 'Hasn't been circulated' → 'hadn't been circulated'. Statement order. Reporting verb: 'demanded to know'.
quests.explanation: Present perfect passive negative → past perfect passive negative. Statement word order is required. 'Demanded to know' suits the forceful nature of the question.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The ethics board said, 'Make sure that all participants give their informed consent before proceeding.'
options: The ethics board required researchers to make sure that all participants gave their informed consent before proceeding.
The ethics board required researchers to make sure that all participants give their informed consent before proceeding.
The ethics board required researchers to make sure all participants had given their informed consent before proceeding.
quests.correctAnswer: The ethics board required researchers to make sure that all participants gave their informed consent before proceeding.
quests.sentence: The ethics board said, 'Make sure that all participants give their informed consent before proceeding.'
quests.hint: 'Give' in the embedded clause → 'gave'. 'Had given' would be an over-shift here.
quests.explanation: 'Make sure' → 'to make sure'. 'Give their consent' → 'gave their consent'. 'Had given' is an over-shift - the original 'give' is present simple, so it shifts to 'gave'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The researcher wrote, 'The results appear to confirm our hypothesis.'
options: The researcher wrote that the results appeared to confirm their hypothesis.
The researcher wrote that the results appear to confirm their hypothesis.
The researcher wrote that the results appeared to have confirmed their hypothesis.
quests.correctAnswer: The researcher wrote that the results appeared to confirm their hypothesis.
quests.sentence: The researcher wrote, 'The results appear to confirm our hypothesis.'
quests.hint: 'Appear' → 'appeared'. 'Our' → 'their'. 'To confirm' stays - no shift in infinitives.
quests.explanation: 'Appear' → 'appeared'. 'Our' → 'their'. The infinitive 'to confirm' stays unchanged. 'To have confirmed' would be an over-shift.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The economist was asked, 'How has globalization affected income inequality?'
options: The economist was asked how globalization had affected income inequality.
The economist was asked how has globalization affected income inequality.
The economist was asked how globalization has affected income inequality.
quests.correctAnswer: The economist was asked how globalization had affected income inequality.
quests.sentence: The economist was asked, 'How has globalization affected income inequality?'
quests.hint: 'Has affected' → 'had affected'. Statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Has affected' (present perfect) → 'had affected' (past perfect). Use statement word order: 'how globalization had affected'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The professor said, 'When citing sources, use the format prescribed by your institution.'
options: The professor told students that when citing sources, they should use the format prescribed by their institution.
The professor told students when citing sources, use the format prescribed by your institution.
The professor told students that when citing sources, you should use the format prescribed by your institution.
quests.correctAnswer: The professor told students that when citing sources, they should use the format prescribed by their institution.
quests.sentence: The professor said, 'When citing sources, use the format prescribed by your institution.'
quests.hint: Imperative with fronted time clause. 'Use' → 'they should use'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: The imperative 'use' → 'they should use' in the that-clause. 'Your institution' → 'their institution'. The participial clause 'when citing sources' stays.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The study concluded, 'The data strongly supports the conclusion that climate change is accelerating.'
options: The study concluded that the data strongly supported the conclusion that climate change was accelerating.
The study concluded that the data strongly supports the conclusion that climate change is accelerating.
The study concluded that the data strongly supported the conclusion that climate change had been accelerating.
quests.correctAnswer: The study concluded that the data strongly supported the conclusion that climate change was accelerating.
quests.sentence: The study concluded, 'The data strongly supports the conclusion that climate change is accelerating.'
quests.hint: 'Supports' → 'supported'. 'Is accelerating' → 'was accelerating'. Both shift.
quests.explanation: Two shifts: 'supports' → 'supported' and 'is accelerating' → 'was accelerating'. 'Had been accelerating' would be an over-shift for the embedded clause.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The researcher asked, 'What percentage of respondents agreed with the statement?'
options: The researcher asked what percentage of respondents had agreed with the statement.
The researcher asked what percentage of respondents agreed with the statement.
The researcher asked what percentage did respondents agree with the statement.
quests.correctAnswer: The researcher asked what percentage of respondents had agreed with the statement.
quests.sentence: The researcher asked, 'What percentage of respondents agreed with the statement?'
quests.hint: 'Agreed' (past simple) → 'had agreed' (past perfect). Statement order.
quests.explanation: Past simple 'agreed' → past perfect 'had agreed'. Use statement word order. Avoid 'did' in reported questions.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The academic supervisor said, 'Cross-reference your findings with existing literature before drawing conclusions.'
options: The academic supervisor instructed the student to cross-reference findings with existing literature before drawing conclusions.
The academic supervisor instructed the student to cross-reference your findings with existing literature before drawing conclusions.
The academic supervisor said cross-reference your findings with existing literature before drawing conclusions.

quests.sentence: The academic supervisor said, 'Cross-reference your findings with existing literature before drawing conclusions.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'instructed + student + to + cross-reference'. 'Your findings' → 'findings' (pronoun dropped as subject is clear).
quests.explanation: 'Cross-reference' → 'to cross-reference'. 'Your findings' becomes 'findings' as the referent is now clear from context.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I've been reconsidering our findings, and I think we may have overlooked something important.'
options: She told the team she had been reconsidering their findings, and she thought they might have overlooked something important.
She told the team she's been reconsidering their findings, and she thinks they may have overlooked something.
She told the team she had been reconsidering their findings, and she thought they may have overlooked something important.
quests.correctAnswer: She told the team she had been reconsidering their findings, and she thought they might have overlooked something important.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I've been reconsidering our findings, and I think we may have overlooked something important.'
quests.hint: 'Have been reconsidering' → 'had been reconsidering'. 'Think' → 'thought'. 'May have' → 'might have'. 'We' → 'they'. 'Our' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: Multiple shifts: 'have been reconsidering' → 'had been reconsidering', 'think' → 'thought', 'may have' → 'might have', 'we' → 'they', 'our' → 'their'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The reviewer asked, 'How robust were the testing procedures used in the study?'
options: The reviewer asked how robust the testing procedures used in the study had been.
The reviewer asked how robust were the testing procedures used in the study.
The reviewer asked how robust the testing procedures had been using in the study.
quests.correctAnswer: The reviewer asked how robust the testing procedures used in the study had been.
quests.sentence: The reviewer asked, 'How robust were the testing procedures used in the study?'
quests.hint: 'Were... robust' → 'the testing procedures had been'. Statement order: adjective complement after 'how'.
quests.explanation: 'Were robust' → 'had been'. Statement word order places the subject before the verb: 'how robust the testing procedures had been'. 'Had been using' is wrong - 'used' is a past participle adjective here.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The standard operating procedure said, 'Document any deviations from the protocol and report them to the supervisor.'
options: The standard operating procedure required researchers to document any deviations from the protocol and report them to the supervisor.
The standard operating procedure required researchers to document any deviations from the protocol and reporting them to the supervisor.
The standard operating procedure said document any deviations from the protocol and report them to the supervisor.
quests.correctAnswer: The standard operating procedure required researchers to document any deviations from the protocol and report them to the supervisor.
quests.sentence: The standard operating procedure said, 'Document any deviations from the protocol and report them to the supervisor.'
quests.hint: Double imperative: 'required + researchers + to + document... and report'. Parallel infinitive structure.
quests.explanation: Two parallel imperatives → 'to document... and report'. Using 'reporting' breaks the parallel infinitive structure.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The report noted, 'The treatment has been more effective for some patients than for others.'
options: The report noted that the treatment had been more effective for some patients than for others.
The report noted that the treatment has been more effective for some patients than others.
The report noted that the treatment was more effective for some patients than for others.

quests.sentence: The report noted, 'The treatment has been more effective for some patients than for others.'
quests.hint: 'Has been' → 'had been'. The comparative structure stays. Note: 'than for others' not 'than others'.
quests.explanation: 'Has been more effective' → 'had been more effective'. The preposition 'for' must be retained: 'than for others'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The peer reviewer asked, 'Were the experimental conditions sufficiently controlled?'
options: The peer reviewer asked whether the experimental conditions had been sufficiently controlled.
The peer reviewer asked whether the experimental conditions were sufficiently controlled.
The peer reviewer asked were the experimental conditions sufficiently controlled.

quests.sentence: The peer reviewer asked, 'Were the experimental conditions sufficiently controlled?'
quests.hint: Past simple passive → past perfect passive. Use 'whether' and statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Were... controlled' (past simple passive) → 'had been... controlled' (past perfect passive). Use 'whether'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The research methodology guide said, 'Situate your research within the broader academic debate.'

The research methodology guide told scholars to situate your research within the broader academic debate.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The team said, 'We acknowledge there are significant limitations to our findings.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The researcher asked, 'At what point did the control group start to show different results?'
options: The researcher asked at what point the control group had started to show different results.
The researcher asked at what point did the control group start to show different results.
The researcher asked at what point the control group started to show different results.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The essay-writing guide said, 'Present your argument clearly and support it with evidence.'

quests.hint: Double imperative: 'advised + students + to + present... and support'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: Two parallel imperatives → 'to present their argument clearly and support it'. 'Your argument' → 'their argument'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The minister said, 'The amendment to the legislation will come into effect next year.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The statistician asked, 'Has the variance in the data been accounted for?'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The lab guide said, 'Identify the key variables and control for confounding factors.'

quests.explanation: 'Identify' and 'control' are parallel imperatives → 'to identify... and control for'. 'To controlling' breaks the parallel infinitive structure.

quests.explanation: 'Believe' → 'believed'. 'Is' → 'was'. In standard reported speech, tense shifts apply even to strongly held beliefs. 'Had been' would be an over-shift.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The examiner asked, 'Which theoretical framework informed your research design?'
